## Step 1 — Quotes

**Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, section 45A — penalty for contravention of provisions or orders where no separate penalty is provided:**

> “Whoever contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or fails to comply with any order or direction given under this Act, for which no penalty has been elsewhere provided in this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both, and in the case of a continuing contravention or failure, with an additional fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day during which such contravention or failure continues after conviction for the first such contravention or failure.” [9]

**Section 43 — cognizability provision identified, but its operative text is not reproduced:**

> “43. Cognizance of offences.” [2][4]

**Section 21 — enforcement procedure identified, but no penalty figures are reproduced:**

> “The above contravention is liable for penalty. Therefore, you are required to show cause within a period of ------ days of service of this notice, why an inquiry should not be initiated against you under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 for imposition of penalty. In case, no reply is received within the given period, the further action shall be taken under the Act.” [5]

**Relevant power of the Board:**

> “Where it is apprehended by a Board that the water in any stream or well is likely to be polluted by reason of the disposal or likely disposal of any matter in such stream or well or in any sewer or on any land, or otherwise, the Board may make an application to a court … for restraining the person who is likely to cause such pollution from so causing.” [16][19]

## Step 2 — Answer

The context does **not** reproduce the substantive provision specifically dealing with “carrying out a polluting process in contravention of an order,” nor does it provide the operative text of section 43 on cognizability. Therefore, it does not establish with certainty either:

1. the maximum penalty applicable to that specific contravention; or  
2. whether that specific offence is cognizable by a court. [2][4][5]

If the relevant contravention is one for which **no penalty is elsewhere provided**, section 45A prescribes imprisonment up to **three months**, or a fine up to **ten thousand rupees**, or both. For a continuing contravention or failure, it also permits an additional fine of up to **five thousand rupees for every day** during which it continues after the first conviction. [9] Section 45A cannot, however, be treated as the governing provision for the specific offence described in the question without the omitted special provision establishing that no other penalty applies. [9]

Section 43 is identified as the **“Cognizance of offences”** provision, but its contents—such as whether cognizance requires a complaint by a Board or is subject to an exception—are missing from the supplied context. Accordingly, the cognezability of the specified offence cannot be determined from these sources. [2][4]
